item.title: What we know so far about the government's plan to end teen deportations
item.description: Sweden's government parties have backed down under pressure on teen deportations, announcing a 'safety clause' to reduce the number of young adults facing deportation after they turn 18. But the details are hazy. Here's what we know so far.

item.title: Sweden's government backs down on deportations in migration u-turn
item.description: Sweden's government has struck an agreement with the far-right Sweden Democrats to stop the deportation of young adults and of foreigners hit by the abolition of the track change law, backing down after a month of heavy media pressure.

item.title: They contribute to Swedish society: Now the government is changing the rules
item.description: Naval architects, fundraising experts, doctors, software engineers, tech entrepreneurs, executive management consultants: meet the people reconsidering their lives and careers in Sweden as a result of the government’s new citizenship laws.

item.title: Ten rules for thriving in a Swedish 'styrelse' board meeting
item.description: When you move to Sweden, the chances are that sooner or later you will be asked to join a 'styrelse' or 'board', whether it's in your apartment block, children's school, or sports club. Here are ten rules to help you survive the next annual meeting.

item.title: How is Sweden reacting to US and Israeli attacks on Iran?
item.description: In this week's podcast: Sweden reacts to attacks on Iran, will Sweden's right soften on immigration? How does speaking Swedish change you? And is it possible to prove your civics knowledge before the new citizenship law kicks in?

item.title: Inside Sweden: Swedish media need to start covering citizenship headaches
item.description: The Local’s Editor Emma Löfgren reflects on her first week back after maternity leave before running through the other stories The Local has covered this week.

item.title: Which countries in Europe impose language tests for residency permits?
item.description: Certain countries across Europe demand foreign citizens pass a language test to qualify for certain residency permits. But how does each country compare and what level of language do they require?

item.title: What we know so far about plans to stop forcing 'track changers' to leave Sweden
item.description: Sweden's government is considering allowing so-called 'track changers' the possibility to apply for a new work permit from within Sweden, instead of having to leave the country and reapply.

item.title: What rights do I have as a second-hand renter in Sweden?
item.description: Renting second-hand in Sweden is tough, with high competition for homes in the big cities and contracts usually limited to a year at most. But the bright side is that you have a lot of rights as a renter in the country – just make sure you know what they are.

item.title: Sweden detains crew member of Russian 'shadow fleet' ship
item.description: Sweden has detained a crew member of a Russian 'shadow fleet' cargo ship suspected of transporting stolen Ukrainian grain, the Swedish coast guard said on Sunday.
